findings.recommendation: Have the close step call it when a script writes the file, or drop it and keep the rule in the docs only.
findings.what: destination() in agent-kit/scripts/findings.py (line 92) states the FINDINGS_TO_ISSUE_AT rule so C1's L, M and C cases are testable, but no script calls it; the orchestrator applies the rule by reading process.md step 9.
findings.how_found: Reading the diff while writing tests/test_findings.py WhereItGoesTest.

findings.recommendation: Raise WORD_CAP in tests/test_orchestrator_comments.py at the next issue that needs words, or move the Close layout into its own page.
findings.what: agent-kit/procedures/orchestrator-comments.md is at 419 of 420 words after trading out about 20 words (the marked-fact aside, two in-this-session phrases and a settings pointer); the next layout change must trade words again.
findings.how_found: wc -w on the file after the C9 edit.

findings.recommendation: Move the sweep entry name pattern into a small shared module when a third script needs it.
findings.what: agent-kit/scripts/findings.py loads sweep-due.py by path only to reuse its ENTRY pattern (line 62), which also imports github_api.py; a change to either script's imports changes findings.py.

findings.recommendation: Refuse a ruling whose `at` is earlier than its entry's `logged` time, or say in formats.md that it is accepted and moves the age anchor before the entry existed.
findings.what: A `kept` ruling dated before the entry's `logged` time is accepted and moves the age anchor back to it (agent-kit/scripts/findings.py apply_rulings lines 247 to 248), so the age would count sweep entries older than the entry itself.
findings.how_found: First QA launch, .scratch/qa200_probe.py, case "kept ruling dated before logged".

findings.recommendation: Check that a ruling's `id` and `ruling` values are text before the dictionary lookups, and catch RecursionError next to JSONDecodeError in parse(), so each prints the one-line refusal.
findings.what: Three inputs make findings.py exit 1 with a Python traceback instead of a one-line refusal naming the file and line or key: a ruling whose `id` is a list or object (line 218), a ruling whose `ruling` is a list (line 210), and a file or ruling line nested thousands of levels deep (json.loads in parse(), line 114).

findings.recommendation: Refuse a rulings path that exists as a link but is not a regular file (use os.path.lexists), and refuse `_docs/records/findings` or `_docs/records` existing as a file.
findings.what: Three odd layouts are skipped silently with exit 0, against C3's "never skips one silently": a rulings file that is a dangling or looping symlink (every closed entry reappears as open), `_docs/records/findings` being a file, and `_docs/records` being a file.

findings.recommendation: Pass the file name through settings.echo (the helper findings.py already uses for ids) in the "must be named" and "only findings files belong here" refusals.
findings.what: The refusal for a badly named file prints the raw path (agent-kit/scripts/findings.py lines 139 to 140 and 188), so a file name holding an escape sequence reaches the terminal unchanged and a name holding a newline splits the one-line refusal into two lines.

findings.recommendation: Match the sweep entry name with ASCII digits (re.ASCII or [0-9]) in sweep-due.py's ENTRY, or recheck the name in findings.py's sweep_times, so only a real timestamp counts.
findings.what: A file named with an Arabic-Indic digit in the year matches sweep-due.py's ENTRY (`\d`, line 43), strptime accepts it, and sweep_times counts it as a sweep, so it ages every open entry by one.

findings.recommendation: Add to process.md step 9 and formats.md (Findings log) that a finding repeated by a re-check or the second launch is logged once, from its latest block, with the group copied unchanged.
findings.what: process.md step 9 and formats.md say the file is written "from the last QA comments' finding blocks", but a re-check repeats a still-open finding with its own id and nothing says to take each id once, so a hand-written file can hold a duplicate id, which `make findings` then refuses.
findings.how_found: Heavy second QA launch, read against the QA comments on #200.
